acceptanceCriteria: The operator-notes spec's rollback section states that full journal audit decodes every historical intent/policy.json POST, so once an accepted policy names NOTE_SET or NOTE_CLEAR (an explicit policy.roles.OPERATOR row or an OWNER row), a binary without those operations fails audit even after a later policy drops them, independent of whether any note was written.
Rollback guidance after such a policy keeps the operation vocabulary and ExplicitGrantOperations and disables only the writer.
A native witness (grant, revoke, audit with the grant removed refuses the historical row) or an explicit NOT_RUN is retained.
body: Found while fixing the same hazard for issue 502 (PR beamfall/corvint#575, commit ec81e4cd, test TestIssue502_OperatorAnswersThroughExplicitGrant). docs/specs/corvint-tasks-operator-notes-v0.md 'Rollout and rollback' says rollback before any note is written reverts the writer, CLI, codec and stage-slot changes. But a policy naming NOTE_SET/NOTE_CLEAR can be committed before any note exists. internal/tasks/journal/records.go validates every historical POST and calls intent.DecodePolicy on intent/policy.json; policy decode checks each role row against intent.Operations and PolicyGrantable (internal/tasks/intent/policy.go:224). A reverted binary therefore fails full audit on that historical policy. Expected: rollback guidance conditioned on whether any accepted policy named the note verbs. Actual: conditioned only on whether a note was written. Version: origin/main 10570f60. Suspected doc defect; the decode path is confirmed by the #502 witness for ESCALATE/ANSWER, not yet witnessed for the note verbs.
title: Operator-notes rollback ignores historical policy audit: a policy naming NOTE_SET blocks a plain revert before any note exists
